html:
A Torres Strait Islander whose court case overturned the idea that Australia had belonged to no one before the British came, and led to the recognition of native title.

Mabo grew up on Mer, or Murray Island, in the eastern Torres Strait. Working as a gardener at a university in Townsville, he was shocked to learn from academics that under Australian law his family's land on Mer belonged to the Crown. He became a campaigner for Indigenous rights.

In 1982 he and four other Meriam men took the state of Queensland to court. The case dragged on for ten years. Mabo died of cancer in January 1992. Five months later, in Mabo v Queensland, the High Court ruled that the doctrine of terra nullius, "land belonging to no one", had been wrong, and that native title to land had survived British settlement.

The decision led to the Native Title Act of 1993 under Paul Keating. It changed how Aboriginal and Islander peoples could claim their country. 3 June, the day of the ruling, is Mabo Day.
sum: A Torres Strait Islander whose court case overturned the idea that Australia had belonged to no one before the British came, and led to the recognition of native title.
